Brown Spot.name: Brown Spot
Brown Spot.description: A fungal disease frequently associated with nutritional stress, silica deficiency, or poorly drained soil conditions.
symptoms: Small circular to oval brown spots uniformly scattered across leaf blades
Mature spots have gray-white centers with distinct yellow halos
Infected seeds turn discolored and shriveled
risk_factors: Nutrient-deficient soils, specifically nitrogen, potassium, and micronutrients like zinc and silica
Drought-stressed upland conditions alternating with wet soil
Use of uncertified farm-saved seed without treatment
precautions: Conduct soil testing and correct nitrogen and potassium deficiencies
Maintain adequate soil moisture without severe drought cycles
Utilize certified treated disease-free seeds
management: Cultural: Practice balanced fertilization with organic manure / compost
Monitoring: Inspect older leaves first as brown spot symptoms initially appear on senescing tissue
Expert Consultation: Obtain soil health card advice from your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra

Bacterial Leaf Blight.name: Bacterial Leaf Blight
Bacterial Leaf Blight.description: A serious bacterial vascular disease causing systemic wilting and wavy yellow-white lesions from leaf tips downward.
symptoms: Water-soaked stripes starting from leaf margins near tips
Lesions turn yellowish to bleached white with undulating, wavy margins
Milky bacterial ooze droplets visible on young lesions during early morning humidity
risk_factors: Continuous rainstorms and strong winds causing leaf abrasion
Deep standing floodwater in lowlands
High nitrogen levels without potassium balance
precautions: Drain excess water from the field during severe weather
Apply balanced fertilizer with split nitrogen and adequate potash
Avoid clipping seedling leaf tips during transplantation
management: Cultural: Plow under crop stubbles immediately after harvest
Monitoring: Check field perimeter every 3 days during tillering stage
Expert Consultation: Connect with district agricultural extension officer

Healthy.name: Healthy
Healthy.description: The rice plant shows vigorous green foliage, uniform leaf color without necrotic lesions, and normal vegetative or reproductive growth.
symptoms: Uniform vibrant green leaves
No discoloration, spots, or lesions
Erect leaf posture and sturdy tillers
risk_factors: Imbalanced nitrogen application may predispose to future infections
Water stagnation or extreme drought
precautions: Continue standard recommended irrigation cycles
Maintain balanced N-P-K nutrient application based on soil testing
Regularly monitor leaf tips and lower canopies
management: Cultural: Keep field bunds clear of wild grasses
Monitoring: Inspect crop twice weekly during panicle initiation
Expert Consultation: Consult local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) for seasonal advisories

Leaf Blast.name: Leaf Blast
Leaf Blast.description: Foliar blast fungus producing classic spindle or diamond-shaped lesions with grayish centers on leaf blades.
symptoms: Spindle-shaped elliptical spots with pointed ends, gray center and dark brown border
Lesions coalesce into large necrotic blighted areas
Severe infection leads to complete leaf drying and burning appearance
risk_factors: Night temperatures around 19-23°C with relative humidity > 90%
Prolonged dew deposition on leaf surfaces
Excessive chemical nitrogen application
precautions: Avoid excessive or late nitrogen application
Maintain optimal plant spacing for ventilation
Plant resistant varieties recommended by agricultural universities
management: Cultural: Destroy infected straw and weeds on field bunds
Monitoring: Scout seedling nurseries and active tillering stages early in the morning
Expert Consultation: Consult local extension officer when lesions cover > 5% leaf area

Leaf Scald.name: Leaf Scald
Leaf Scald.description: Fungal disease characterized by prominent zonate banding starting from leaf tips and margins resembling scalded tissue.
symptoms: Water-soaked oblong lesions developing from leaf tips and outer margins
Concentric alternating light tan and dark reddish-brown bands
Leaf tips dry up and take on a bleached, shredded appearance
risk_factors: High humidity, frequent rain showers, and warm temperatures (25-30°C)
Dense canopy with poor air circulation
High nitrogen levels and close planting
precautions: Avoid excessive nitrogen; apply potassium in split doses
Space hills at recommended distance (e.g., 20 x 15 cm)
Keep field bunds weed-free
management: Cultural: Practice crop rotation and clear stubble post-harvest
Monitoring: Check upper canopy leaves after prolonged rainy spells
Expert Consultation: Contact local KVK agronomist if scald bands advance to flag leaves

Narrow Brown Spot.name: Narrow Brown Spot
Narrow Brown Spot.description: Fungal leaf disease producing short, narrow, linear reddish-brown lesions parallel to leaf veins.
symptoms: Short, narrow, linear brown spots (2-10 mm long, 1-1.5 mm wide) parallel to leaf veins
Uniform light to dark brown spots without gray centers
Causes premature leaf drying and poor grain filling
risk_factors: Nutrient-depleted soils, especially potassium deficiency
Warm and humid late-season weather during heading
Susceptible late-maturing varieties
precautions: Ensure balanced potassium nutrition according to soil tests
Avoid delayed sowing in late seasons
Select resistant cultivars
management: Cultural: Remove infected residues after harvesting
Monitoring: Inspect flag leaf from panicle emergence onwards
Expert Consultation: Seek guidance if lesions appear before 50% heading

Neck Blast.name: Neck Blast
Neck Blast.description: Destructive phase of blast disease where the fungus attacks the neck node supporting the panicle, causing chaffy grains or broken heads.
symptoms: Brownish-black necrotic lesion at the neck node of the panicle
Panicle neck becomes brittle and snaps
Grains remain empty, chaffy, and whitish (whitehead effect)
risk_factors: Foliar leaf blast present in the vegetative stage with spore splash during heading
Intermittent rains and heavy morning dew during panicle emergence
Over-fertilization with nitrogen near heading
precautions: Strictly avoid nitrogen top-dressing after boot leaf emergence
Maintain proper water depth without excessive inundation
Adopt community-wide blast-resistant cultivars
management: Cultural: Rogue severely infected neck blast panicles
Monitoring: Inspect panicle emergence daily in humid weather
Expert Consultation: Report neck blast emergence immediately to agricultural officers

Rice Hispa.name: Rice Hispa
Rice Hispa.description: Destructive insect pest where spiny beetles scrape upper leaf surfaces and larvae mine between leaf layers.
symptoms: Parallel white streaks on upper leaf surface scraped by adult beetles
White blotches or blister mines created by larvae inside leaf tissue
Damaged leaves wither giving the field a scorched, whitish appearance
risk_factors: Heavy continuous rain followed by sunny days during tillering
Dense grassy weeds on bunds serving as alternate hosts
High seedling density in nursery beds
precautions: Clip seedling leaf tips before transplanting to destroy eggs and grubs
Maintain clean field bunds and destroy wild host grasses
Avoid excessive plant density
management: Cultural: Sweep nets to collect and eliminate adult beetles
Monitoring: Count adults and damaged leaves per hill during active tillering
Expert Consultation: Alert agricultural department if damage exceeds 1 adult per hill

Sheath Blight.name: Sheath Blight
Sheath Blight.description: Fungal disease characterized by greenish-gray oval lesions on leaf sheaths near the water line.
symptoms: Oval or irregular water-soaked spots on leaf sheaths just above water level
Lesions turn grayish-white with irregular brown boundaries
Infection progresses upward to flag leaves forming banded lesions
risk_factors: Warm temperatures (28-32°C) and high relative humidity (85-100%)
Heavy canopy density and high nitrogen levels
Excessive vegetative growth
precautions: Optimize seedling spacing for canopy aeration
Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer; split into 3-4 doses
Drain field water intermittently to lower moisture around sheath base
management: Cultural: Remove weed hosts like Echinochloa on field bunds
Field Management: Skim floating sclerotia during final puddling
Expert Consultation: Check with local agronomist if >20% hills show sheath lesions

Tungro.name: Tungro
Tungro.description: Viral disease complex transmitted by green leafhoppers leading to severe stunting and orange-yellow discoloration.
symptoms: Stunted plants with significantly reduced tillering
Leaves turn yellow to orange-yellow starting from leaf tips
Young leaves show mottled or interveinal chlorosis
risk_factors: Presence of Green Leafhopper vector populations
Staggered planting in adjacent fields harboring continuous vectors
Susceptible varieties planted during high vector migration
precautions: Practice synchronous planting within the farming village
Eradicate volunteer rice plants and wild grass hosts during fallow
Grow tungro-resistant rice varieties
management: Cultural: Light traps to monitor leafhopper vector density
Monitoring: Scout nursery beds and early tillering for green leafhoppers
Expert Consultation: Report yellow stunting immediately to agricultural authorities
